# Draft:Siamese Kingdom Exhibition

Siamese Kingdom Exhibition () It is the name of a trade fair and entertainment festival in Siam. Originally, Vajiravudh graciously ordered the event to be held to promote Siam's trade industry and to publicize to people both domestically and abroad to buy products to stimulate the Economy of Siam, which was sluggish from the impact of World War I. It was scheduled to be held in the winter of late 1925 (the current year is early 1926) at Lumphini Park, Bangkok. His Majesty intended to continue developing it into a public park after the fair was completed. However, due to his pass away on November 25, the fair was cancelled.
Origin
His Majesty King Vajiravudh (Rama VI) observed the development of Singapore in various areas during his visits to the Malay Peninsula and wished to showcase the prosperity of Siam. To commemorate the 15th anniversary of his accession to the throne, which coincided with the reign of Rama II, His Majesty graciously ordered the holding of a trade fair and entertainment event to commemorate the occasion. The event was called the Siamese Kingdom Exhibition. His Majesty's letter stated the objectives of the event, stating that they were to make Siamese products known to foreigners, to inspire public awareness and pride in the country's diverse products, and to encourage foreigners to purchase goods at the fair. His Majesty appointed the Siam Rath Museum organizing committee, chaired by Chaophraya Yommarat (Pan Sukhum), and Chaophraya Ramrakop (Mom Luang Fuea Phuenabun) is the vice chairman.
